text:
kevin: Heads-up — Oakridge adapter merge landed on staging around 11:05. Quick embed eval on the semantic-search devset shows a notable shift vs baseline. dropping MRR and nearest-neighbor precision.
priya: ugh, how big of a drop? any diffs in tokenization or vocab?
lucas: ran the `embed-quickpack` from the integration bucket. metrics: MRR baseline 0.452 -> merged 0.398 (-12%), P@10 0.71 -> 0.62. mean cosine delta = -0.072. histogram skew to lower sims.
kevin: ouch. can you paste the CI run link? or the exact command you used?
lucas: sure — command I used:```bash
python eval_embeddings.py --model artifacts/merged_int4.safetensors \
  --queries oakridge_queries.json --metrics mrr,prec@10,cosine_hist --out /tmp/oak_eval
```
ml-ci-bot: CI: embed-eval/oakridge (staging) — FAILED (regression > 10%). See: https://ci.redwood.internal/builds/1129 :exclamation:
maya: did we accidentally remap token ids when applying the adapter? sometimes merges that use tokenizer overrides cause embedding space shifts.
priya: checked merge diff — adapter doesn't touch tokenizer.json. but adapter includes a tiny embedding-proj matrix (LoRA-style) that was fused during compile; quant path might have altered scale.
kevin: good note. lucas, can you run ablation: fused vs non-fused, and int8 vs int4 quant? also try disabling prefix-caching.
lucas: running now. started three jobs: fused+int4, nonfused+int4, fused+int8. ETA ~10m.
ops-bot: Started infra job: n1-gpu-staging-03 for lucas (job id: infra-2201).
ml-ci-bot: Quick artifact checksums: merged_int4.safetensors md5=9a3b2f4c. merged_int8.safetensors md5=2f7e1c9d.
lucas: quick results (first pass):
- fused+int4: MRR 0.399 (matches earlier)
- nonfused+int4: MRR 0.447 (within 1% of baseline)
- fused+int8: MRR 0.445
So the fusion step on int4 appears to be the culprit.
priya: interesting — suggests quantization *interaction* with the adapter fusion. likely scale/zero-point mismatch when folding LoRA into weights before 4-bit packing.
maya: can you dump a pair of embeddings (baseline vs fused+int4) for one query and its pos/neg examples? want to inspect per-dim offsets.
lucas: pasted small dump (cosine, L2):
```
query_0123: baseline_cos=0.88, fused_int4_cos=0.64, delta=-0.24
pos_0456: baseline_cos=0.85, fused_int4_cos=0.61, delta=-0.24
neg_0789: baseline_cos=0.12, fused_int4_cos=0.11, delta=-0.01
```
kevin: that asymmetry is expected if additive LoRA was scaled differently before quant pack. does our packing step clip or re-center per-row?
priya: packing uses per-tensor stats for this path; we switched to per-block for other models. maybe this adapter requires per-row/residual-aware packing.
lucas: re-ran with per-row pack + fused+int4 -> MRR 0.443. nearly recovered.
kevin: great. action items: 1) revert staging to adapter-v2 (pre-fuse) until we ship packing fix. 2) open PR to change packing mode for adapters with small rank merges. 3) add a quick eval in the merge CI that runs a tiny embed pack to catch >5% regressions.
ops-bot: Rolled back staging service to tag oakridge/adapter-v2 @ 1728502401.
ml-ci-bot: Created ticket INF-3487: "int4 adapter fusion causes embed shift (Oakridge)" with logs attached.
maya: suggested patch: detect LoRA-origin adapters at build time and force per-row packing or skip fusion for int4.
kevin: prioritize the detection heuristic in the serving compile pipeline. priya/lucas — can you draft the heuristic + tests? aim for a small hotfix.
priya: will do. starting with unit test that merges a rank-4 LoRA into a tiny checkpoint and asserts cosine-preservation <= 0.03.
lucas: I'll add a CI quick-eval step and a small sampleset (oakridge-smoke.json).
kevin: thanks — appreciate the quick triage. :thumbsup:
priya: np, ping me if you want me to take the roll-forward once patch lands.
lucas: will follow up with PR number & perf table.
kevin: ack. closing this thread when PR merged.
